74062-the-magazine-of-history-with-notes.creator: Unknown
74062-the-magazine-of-history-with-notes.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Prior to the outbreak of the Revolution the militia of the Province of Massachusetts Bay was governed by the provisions of an act for regulating the militia, passed in 1693. Although quaint and antiquated in its provisions, it seems to have sufficed for all practical purposes; and no other act was passed regulating the militia until the Provincial Congress, almost at the beginning of its sittings, took steps to place the militia of the Province upon a different basis in order to find themselves

arxiv-2107-11830.title: Critical and geometric properties of magnetic polymers across the globule-coil transition
arxiv-2107-11830.creator: Kamilla Faizullina, Ilya Pchelintsev, Evgeni Burovski
arxiv-2107-11830.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kamilla Faizullina, Ilya Pchelintsev, Evgeni Burovski. We study a lattice model of a single magnetic polymer chain, where Ising spins are located on the sites of a lattice self-avoiding walk in d = 2 d=2 . We consider the regime where both conformations and magnetic degrees of freedom are dynamic, thus the Ising model is defined on a dynamic lattice and conformations generate an annealed disorder.

arxiv-2109-01239.title: A Max-Min Task Offloading Algorithm for Mobile Edge Computing Using Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access Thanks: Vaibhav Kumar and Le-Nam Tran are with the School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, University College Dublin, D04 V1W8 Dublin, Ireland. (email: vaibhav.kumar@ieee.org, nam.tran@ucd.ie)
arxiv-2109-01239.creator: Vaibhav Kumar, Muhammad Fainan Hanif
arxiv-2109-01239.description: Abstract To mitigate the computational power gap between the network core and edges, mobile edge computing (MEC) is poised to play a fundamental role in future generations of wireless networks. In this correspondence, we consider a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) transmission model to maximize the worst task to be offloaded among all users to the network edge server.

arxiv-2111-14036.title: Pre-training Recommender Systems via Reinforced Attentive Multi-relational Graph Neural Network
arxiv-2111-14036.creator: Xiaohan Li 2 , Zhiwei Liu 2 , Stephen Guo 3 , Zheng Liu 2 , Hao Peng 4 , Philip S. Yu 2 , Kannan Achan 3
arxiv-2111-14036.description: Abstract Recently, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven their effectiveness for recommender systems. Existing studies have applied GNNs to capture collaborative relations in the data. However, in real-world scenarios, the relations in a recommendation graph can be of various kinds. For example, two movies may be associated either by the same genre or by the same director/actor.

arxiv-2210-15381.title: Quantum multiparameter estimation with multi-mode photon catalysis entangled squeezed state
arxiv-2210-15381.creator: Huan Zhang 1, Wei Ye 2, Shoukang Chang 3, Ying Xia 1, Liyun Hu 4, Zeyang Liao 1
arxiv-2210-15381.description: Abstract We propose a method to generate the multi-mode entangled catalysis squeezed vacuum states (MECSVS) by embedding the cross-Kerr nonlinear medium into the Mach-Zehnder interferometer. This method realizes the exchange of quantum states between different modes based on Fredkin gate. In addition, we study the MECSVS as the probe state of multi-arm optical interferometer to realize multi-phase simultaneous estimation.

arxiv-2211-11713.title: On the monotonicity of a quantum optimal transport cost
arxiv-2211-11713.creator: Alexander Müller-Hermes
arxiv-2211-11713.description: Abstract . We show that the quantum generalization of the 2 2 -Wasserstein distance proposed by Chakrabarti et al. is not monotone under partial traces. This disproves a recent conjecture by Friedland et al. Finally, we propose a stabilized version of the original definition, which we show to be monotone under the application of general quantum channels.

arxiv-2302-08026.title: Predicting Gender and Political Affiliation Using Mobile Payment Data
arxiv-2302-08026.creator: Ben Stobaugh, Dhiraj Murthy
arxiv-2302-08026.description: Abstract We explore the understudied area of social payments to evaluate whether or not we can predict the gender and political affiliation of Venmo users based on the content of their Venmo transactions. Latent attribute detection has been successfully applied in the domain of studying social media. However, there remains a dearth of previous work using data other than Twitter.

arxiv-2303-01420.title: ArtPlanner: Robust Legged Robot Navigation in the Field Thanks: This work was supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNF) through the NCCR Robotics and project 188596, and the EU Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreements No 780883, No 852044 and No 101016970.
arxiv-2303-01420.creator: Lorenz Wellhausen, Marco Hutter
arxiv-2303-01420.description: Abstract Due to the highly complex environment present during the DARPA Subterranean Challenge, all six funded teams relied on legged robots as part of their robotic team. Their unique locomotion skills of being able to step over obstacles require special considerations for navigation planning.

arxiv-2404-14655.title: Geometric Optimization of Restricted-Open and Complete Active Space Self-Consistent Field Wavefunctions
arxiv-2404-14655.creator: Laurent Vidal, Tommaso Nottoli, Filippo Lipparini, Eric Cancès
arxiv-2404-14655.description: Abstract We explore Riemannian optimization methods for Restricted-Open-shell Hartree-Fock (ROHF) and Complete Active Space Self-Consistent Field (CASSCF) methods. After showing that ROHF and CASSCF can be reformulated as optimization problems on so-called flag manifolds, we review Riemannian optimization basics and their application to these specific problems.

arxiv-2408-09451.title: GraphSPNs: Sum-Product Networks Benefit From Canonical Orderings
arxiv-2408-09451.creator: Milan Papež, Martin Rektoris, Václav Šmídl, Tomáš Pevný
arxiv-2408-09451.description: Abstract Deep generative models have recently made remarkable progress in capturing complex probability distributions over graphs. However, they are intractable and thus unable to answer even the most basic probabilistic inference queries without resorting to approximations. Therefore, we propose graph sum-product networks (GraphSPNs), a tractable deep generative model that provides exact and efficient inference over (arbitrary parts of) graphs.

arxiv-2409-15187.title: Loopy Movements: Emergence of Rotation in a Multicellular Robot Thanks: 1 The authors are with the Department of Mechanical, Materials, and Aerospace Engineering, West Virginia University, Morgantown, WV 26505, USA Affiliation: Trevor Smith, Yu Gu West Virginia University Morgantown, USA Thanks: 2 T
arxiv-2409-15187.description: Abstract Unlike most human-engineered systems, many biological systems rely on emergent behaviors from low-level interactions, enabling greater diversity and superior adaptation to complex, dynamic environments. This study explores emergent decentralized rotation in the Loopy multicellular robot, composed of homogeneous, physically linked, 1-degree-of-freedom cells.

arxiv-2412-00578.title: Speedy-Splat: Fast 3D Gaussian Splatting with Sparse Pixels and Sparse Primitives
arxiv-2412-00578.creator: Alex Hanson, Allen Tu, Geng Lin, Vasu Singla, Tom Goldstein
arxiv-2412-00578.description: Abstract 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D-GS) is a recent 3D scene reconstruction technique that enables real-time rendering of novel views by modeling scenes as parametric point clouds of differentiable 3D Gaussians. However, its rendering speed and model size still present bottlenecks, especially in resource-constrained settings.

arxiv-2501-08485.title: FORMULATION OF A NEW SIR MODEL WITH NON-LOCAL MOBILITY
arxiv-2501-08485.creator: Ciana Applegate, Jiaxu Li, Dan Han
arxiv-2501-08485.description: Abstract In this manuscript, we develop a mobility-based Susceptible-Infectious-Recovered (SIR) model to elucidate the dynamics of pandemic propagation. While traditional SIR models within the field of epidemiology aptly characterize transitions among susceptible, infected, and recovered states, they typically neglect the inherent spatial mobility of particles.

arxiv-2504-03939.title: Deep Learning-Enhanced Robotic Subretinal Injection with Real-Time Retinal Motion Compensation
arxiv-2504-03939.creator: Tianle Wu, Mojtaba Esfandiari, Peiyao Zhang, Russell H. Taylor, Peter Gehlbach, Iulian Iordachita
arxiv-2504-03939.description: Abstract Subretinal injection is a critical procedure for delivering therapeutic agents to treat retinal diseases such as age-related macular degeneration (AMD). However, retinal motion caused by physiological factors such as respiration and heartbeat significantly impacts precise needle positioning, increasing the risk of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) damage.

arxiv-2510-00696.title: Machine Learning-based Path Loss Prediction in Suburban Environment in the Sub-6 GHz Band
arxiv-2510-00696.creator: Ferdaous Tarhouni, Muneer Al-Zubi, Member, IEEE, Mohamed-Slim Alouini, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2510-00696.description: Abstract Accurate path loss (PL) prediction is crucial for successful network planning, antenna design, and performance optimization in wireless communication systems. Several conventional approaches for PL prediction have been adopted, but they have been demonstrated to lack flexibility and accuracy.

arxiv-2603-10171.title: States of 2D Yang-Mills and Large-Volume Entanglement
arxiv-2603-10171.creator: Dmitry Melnikov, Jefferson T. Oliveira, Valmir Peixoto, Marcia Tenser

arxiv-2604-08072.title: Tensor‑Augmented Convolutional Neural Networks: Enhancing Expressivity with Generic Tensor Kernels
arxiv-2604-08072.creator: Chia-Wei Hsing, Wei-Lin Tu

pmc-10737819.title: USE OF PRESCRIPTION MEDICATIONS WITH SOMNOLENCE AS A POTENTIAL ADVERSE EFFECT AMONG OLDER ADULTS IN THE UNITED STATES
pmc-10737819.creator: Jocelyn Wilder
pmc-10737819.description: Over half of community-dwelling older adults experience sleep disorders, with approximately 40% reporting somnolence or/and excessive daytime sleepiness, associated with an increased risk for cognitive impairment and premature mortality. The use and concurrent use of prescription medication with somnolence as an adverse effect may be an overlooked contributor to this growing problem.

pmc-11018324.title: Effects of fullerene C60 on liver tissue in liver ischemia reperfusion injury in rats undergoing sevoflurane anesthesia
pmc-11018324.creator: Aydın Yavuz, Ayca Tas Tuna, Cagrı Ozdemir, Tülay Mortas, Ayşegül Küçük, Esat Kasapbaşı, Mustafa Arslan, Mustafa Kavutçu, Ömer Kurtipek
pmc-11018324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study aimed to investigate the effects of fullerene C60 on rat liver tissue in a liver ischemia reperfusion injury (IRI) model under sevoflurane anesthesia to evaluate the ability of nanoparticles to prevent hepatic complications.

pmc-11369538.title: Extraction of Substance Use Information From Clinical Notes: Generative Pretrained Transformer–Based Investigation
pmc-11369538.creator: Fatemeh Shah-Mohammadi, Joseph Finkelstein, Alexandre Castonguay, Terry Church, Yiyang Liu
pmc-11369538.description: BackgroundUnderstanding the multifaceted nature of health outcomes requires a comprehensive examination of the social, economic, and environmental determinants that shape individual well-being. Among these determinants, behavioral factors play a crucial role, particularly the consumption patterns of psychoactive substances, which have important implications on public health.

pmc-12658130.title: ACA kills Mycobacterium tuberculosis and M. bovis by targeting cell wall core assembling protein CpsA
pmc-12658130.creator: Feng Huang, Mengcong Shi, Liu Chen, Xiaohui Li, Zixin Wang, Dong Jiang, Junfeng Chen, Hua Zhang, Zheng-Guo He
pmc-12658130.description: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, still globally threatens human health. With the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains, there is an imperative need to discover new anti-TB agents and identify novel drug targets. Here, we report that the compound ACA, namely 3-azidothiophene-2-carboxylic acid, can kill M. tuberculosis by targeting the bacterial cell wall core assembling process.

pmc-12980260.title: Hydrothermal Carbonization of Sucrose into Hydrochar: Insights into Surface Chemistry for Efficient Removal of Cationic Dyes
pmc-12980260.creator: Pacharaphon Khaopueak, Kanokorn Wechakorn
pmc-12980260.description: Synthetic dyes, which are extensively used in textile and other industries, produce wastewater that is toxic, recalcitrant, and non-biodegradable. As such, environmental concerns are drawing attention to sustainable adsorbents of the dyes. In this study, hydrochar was green-synthesized using table sugar (sucrose) via hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) at 200 °C for 12 h without toxic additives.

pmc-13311962.title: Dynamic urinary proteomics integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to reveal tumour microenvironment and predict immunotherapy response in biliary tract cancer
pmc-13311962.creator: Shanshan Wang, Zhengguang Guo, Boyu Sun, Kai Liu, Jiashuo Chao, Ziyu Xun, Yunchao Wang, Zibo Xu, Ziyue Huang, Hao Wang, Yang Tan, Nan Zhang, Mingjian Piao, Longhao Zhang, Chengjie Li, Shuofeng Li, Jiongyuan Li, Haidan Sun, Feng Qi, Aiwei Wang, XiaoBo Yang, Chengpei Zhu, Hanping Wang, Wei Sun, Haitao
pmc-13311962.description: BackgroundMost patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC) do not derive durable clinical benefit (DCB) from immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), underscoring the urgent need for predictive biomarkers. While urinary proteomics represents a non-invasive approach for biomarker discovery and mechanism exploration, its utility in ICI-treated patients with cancer remains unexplored.

pmc-13347604.title: Multi-shot diffusion tensor imaging in the lumbosacral spinal cord: Characterizing heterogeneity in healthy tissue and differences in multiple sclerosis
pmc-13347604.creator: Alicia E. Cronin, Xinyu Zhang, Anna Combes, Simon Vandekar, Gabriella L. Dunay, Lipika Narisetti, Grace Sweeney, Logan Prock, Delaney Houston, Aimee Salakhov, Kurt G. Schilling, Seth Stubblefield, Colin D. McKnight, Francesca Bagnato, Subramaniam Sriram, Seth A. Smith, Kristin P. O’Grady
pmc-13347604.description: The clinical presentation of lower extremity and autonomic dysfunction of persons with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) does not consistently correlate with central nervous system pathology noted on conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) could provide more information about tissue microstructure and insight into pathophysiology but is understudied in relevant anatomies such as the lumbosacral spinal cord (LSC).

pmc-13415677.title: High perceived energy: exploring distinct patterns of energetic and cognitive functioning in older adults
pmc-13415677.creator: Orsola Marra, Diego Primavera, Giulia Cossu, Alessandra Perra, Michela Atzeni, Elisa Pintus, Massimo Tusconi, Gianluca Castelnuovo, Maria Veronica Brasesco, Gustavo Mausel, Mauro Giovanni Carta
pmc-13415677.description: BackgroundA hyperthymic temperament and high perceived energy are often framed as positive dispositional traits, particularly in later life. Indeed, these characteristics are generally associated with a greater tendency to preserve autonomy and with more favorable outcomes in terms of health, engagement, and participation in community life-key dimensions of successful aging.

pmc-13527815.title: Self-Medication Practices in Nigeria: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13527815.creator: Chibuzor G. Muoka, Nnedimma V. Akparanta, Favour A. Taribo, Chiemela O. Onubogu, David A. Asiegbu, Chidubem J. Azubike, Iheomachi O. Nwokoro, Chukwuebuka E. Athan, Ugwunna Ede, Emmanuel I. Uwaechina
pmc-13527815.description: Background:Self-medication is a common health-seeking practice in Nigeria and is associated with inappropriate medicine use, adverse drug reactions, and antimicrobial resistance. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of self-medication in Nigeria and synthesize evidence on its patterns, determinants, and consequences.

pmc-13530345.title: Artificial intelligence in prostate MRI: Comparative diagnostic performance in a high-prevalence cohort
pmc-13530345.creator: Nádia Gonçalves Ferreira, Owen Matthew Truscott Thomas, Kjell-Inge Gjesdal, Stig Müller, Jan Oldenburg, Ingrid Framås Syversen, Anders Christian Hansen, Jonn Terje Geitung

pmc-13538947.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Electromechanical Window Negativity in Congenital Long QT Syndrome
pmc-13538947.creator: Toby Paterson, Roy Sanders, Vivetha Pooranachandran
pmc-13538947.description: Risk stratification in congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS) continues to rely heavily on genotype and QTc duration, despite their limited ability to identify individuals at highest arrhythmic risk. The electromechanical window (EMW) is a validated marker of malignant arrhythmia susceptibility, yet its presence within routine echocardiographic imaging has not been recognized.

pmc-13556723.title: 614. Aberrant functional connectivity in children with DMDD and ADHD
pmc-13556723.creator: P-Y Pan, C-B Yeh
pmc-13556723.description: BackgroundDisruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD) is impairing among children and adolescents, and is associated with long-term negative psychiatric outcomes, including unipolar depression and anxiety. One of the main characteristics of DMDD is chronic irritability, a proneness to extraordinary emotional reactions during frustrating condition.

pmc-13587721.title: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome associated with Rickettsia conorii infection: a rare case report
pmc-13587721.creator: Hamidreza Naderi, Alireza Sedaghat, AbouSaleh Sobhi, Mohammadreza Seyedzadeh, Hamidreza Mirzaei, Parsa Aryanpour, Saber Esmaeili
pmc-13587721.description: Highlights•Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare neurological disorder characterized by headaches, seizures, and visual symptoms.•Rickettsia conorii is an infectious cause of PRES.•Rickettsial infections should be considered in atypical cases of PRES.•Intravenous ciprofloxacin may be an alternative when doxycycline cannot be administered.

pmc-13606213.title: Arabidopsis TPXL Proteins Mediate a Selective Aurora Kinase–Microtubule Association During Cell Division
pmc-13606213.creator: Shilin Cao, Yuying Chen, Zongkuan Weng, Haiyun Ren, Pingzhou Du
pmc-13606213.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microtubule organization during cell division requires coordinated regulation by microtubule-associated proteins and protein kinase signaling pathways. In animals, TPX2 (Targeting Protein for Xklp2) regulates spindle assembly by binding to and activating Aurora A kinase. In Arabidopsis, individual TPX2-like (TPXL) proteins have been implicated in Aurora-associated functions, but whether the TPXL family members share common microtubule-associated properties and how TPXL-Aurora interactions differ across the family remain incompletely understood.

pmc-13619392.title: The Medicine Success fund: financial support for widening participation medical students improves wellbeing and increases sense of belonging
pmc-13619392.creator: Brigit McWade, Sarah Marsden, Charlotte Ross, Amina Iqbal
pmc-13619392.description: BackgroundUK medicine is an elite profession engaging in widening participation (WP) efforts to diversify the workforce so as to better represent the society it serves, and thus, enhance patient care. Despite years of sector-wide efforts, medical students and doctors from disadvantaged socio-economic backgrounds remain minoritised in medicine.

pmc-13633631.title: Evaluating tuberculosis service accessibility in Pakistan by analyzing population movement patterns from telecom mobility and survey data
pmc-13633631.creator: Christina Mergenthaler, Oluwafemi John Ifejube, Peter Stephens, Razi Syed, Yee Theng Ng, Umar Saif, Bilal Butt, Frank Cobelens, Ente Rood
pmc-13633631.description: BackgroundGeographical distance is an important dimension of access to healthcare and is considered in a wide range of settings to aid strategic planning and evaluation of healthcare interventions. Evidence has shown that in addition to geographic distance, multiple factors influence the travel behavior of people seeking health services.
